retrospective.harder_than_needed: The exact 0.7.0 ingest() result union and event payload shapes are not inferable from the installed 0.5.1-era app source; they had to be read from the fork's built .d.ts. The lead pre-supplied them in the brief, which removed the friction — without that, the architect would have had to reverse-engineer the union from node_modules.
retrospective.surprised_by: The fork emits BOTH applicationMessage and authenticatedApplicationMessage for the same authenticated message from adjacent lines, so listening to both would double-process — the single-listener switch (not addition) is load-bearing and easy to get subtly wrong.

summary: Wired the marmot-ts 0.7.0 library-authenticated MLS sender through the dispatcher seam. The single inbound-message listener now subscribes to 'authenticatedApplicationMessage' (not the raw 'applicationMessage' event) and builds sender.authenticity:'mls' directly from the library-supplied senderPubkey, replacing the inert 'claimed' stub. Widened epochResolver.ts's MlsGroupLike to the fork's IngestResult union (tsc now clean). Wired the library's unauthenticatedMessage diagnostic to a visible console.warn. Retired the authenticatedSenderResolver stub (Seam B1). Verified — without code change — that the S6 announcement gate (chatHandler.ts) and leaveHandler.ts's forced-removal guard now check a genuinely authenticated sender.
